text:
Three weeks after Winnipeg traded Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey, the Jets are on the best run of their season. They've won five straight, outscored teams 27-14, and won the chance battle every time, with 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) over the stretch. Thursday in Dallas they fell two goals behind and won 8-3. Dawson Mercer, who arrived in the Hellebuyck trade, scored twice against his old team on Tuesday, and Daily Faceoff noted that Mark Scheifele has now tied the franchise points record. Stuart Skinner, the man replacing a Vezina winner, is at .886 but slightly better than his shots deserved (+1.2).

Chicago spent its week answering a harder question. General manager Kyle Davidson talked for nearly 45 minutes on Wednesday, took responsibility for a start that isn't what the team promised, and said Jeff Blashill stays, with "full confidence," as the Daily Herald reported. Connor Bedard said the players have "100 percent belief" in the coach (NHL.com). Then the Blackhawks beat Buffalo 3-2 in overtime on Ryan Donato's goal, snapping a six-game winless run, with Patrick Kane back from injured reserve. It was one night. They're still 1-4-0 in their last five, outscored 25-11, and have 41% of the five-on-five expected goals this season.

Our numbers say they're a bit better than their record: a -36 goal difference on -18.4 expected, with finishing (8.1 goals short) and goaltending (9.5 goals allowed above expected) doing extra damage. Spencer Knight, +11.1 last season, is at -1.9. Bowen Byram is still out, practicing in a non-contact jersey, per Mark Lazerus of The Athletic.

Kyle Connor is two points from 700, and our numbers have him at 49% to score, the best in this game. Scheifele has points in five straight and ten in his last five against Chicago. On the other side, Roman Kantserov carries a nine-game point streak and is one of our Sleepers at 58% for a point. These teams met on Oct. 15, and Chicago won 4-3 in overtime.
headline: The Jets keep winning; the Blackhawks keep their coach
